properties.name: FIELD REPORT (a work project, 2026-09-14): "6 structural findings and 1 undispositioned drift" reached the user verbatim — reflow2's own jargon, not the user's language, despite the lens/persona that exists to prevent exactly this. Anthony: root-cause WHY the lens is not filtering it; a baseball coach would give up here
properties.statement:
RELAYED by Anthony from a project at his workplace, 2026-09-14. The agent's closing line to him, verbatim: "Remaining: 6 structural findings and 1 undispositioned drift (the deleted [file], outstanding since before this session). Both are the check-health workflow rather than this one — and its repair step can delete nodes, so it's worth reading what it proposes rather than applying blind."

ANTHONY, in his words: "My brother stated that he doesn't know the reflow2 jargon. I agree — when I see this the first question that comes to mind is: what is a structural finding and what is an undispositioned drift? We had introduced a 'lens' that is supposed to account for who the user is and their background so that it presents things back to the user in their natural language. My brother has a friend who is a baseball coach — if he saw something like this, he'd probably give up using reflow2 because it isn't something he would understand. This is significant enough that we need to do a /root-cause on why reflow2 jargon continues to appear back to the user and why it isn't filtered through the lens or persona of the user."

WHAT IS ON THE RECORD ALREADY, so the root cause starts from precedent and not from scratch: cap:the-register-rule-reaches-the-words ("the domain-register rule reaches every reply and the exact step where the user's question is written — and it is lint-checked"); dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply (OPEN); the served skills' `lens` block ("Speak the reader's domain, never reflow2's… a vocabulary swap, not simplification"); rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word's neighbour on register; and Anthony's recurring correction that Alex is a user who does not know the jargon. The register rule EXISTS, is lint-checked, and this sentence reached him anyway — so the question is not "is there a rule" but WHERE THE RULE FAILS TO REACH: is the lint checking skill TEXT while the offending words come from TOOL REPLIES (`loop_status`'s `structural_defects`, `undispositioned_drift` are FIELD NAMES the agent read out); does the lens block reach the agent at the moment it WRITES THE CLOSING SUMMARY (a moment no skill governs); does the persona have a recorded background for that user at all (a lens with no recorded reader falls back to nothing).

THE ROOT-CAUSE TO RUN NEXT SESSION, with the skill and its bones: ① symptom as observation (the sentence above; expected: "6 things about the design's shape to look at, and 1 file the design still lists that was deleted"; not affected: the same agent's gap questions, which ARE rephrased via gap_to_prompt). ② precedent (above). ③ bones: INTENT (which requirement says replies are in the user's register, and is it accepted); ALLOCATION (where the register rule is enforced — skill lint on SKILL.md text vs the served tool reply field names); CONTRACT (loop_status's reply is a contract full of reflow2 nouns and nothing translates them); ASSURANCE (what verifies the lens — probably a lint on skill prose, never a test on what a user READS); CHANGE (when the lens shipped and what it covered). ④ the discriminating measurement: take the exact tool reply the agent summarised and ask which words in the user's sentence came from field names vs skill text. ⑥ the class: reflow2 nouns in reply FIELDS and gap TITLES are read out by agents as if they were English — the lens governs prose the SKILLS write, not prose the TOOLS return.

WHAT WOULD ADDRESS IT is the root cause's to say — recorded here only that the fix must reach the words a person actually reads, and that the baseball coach is the test.
